/SUNDAY NIGHT THROUGH THURSDAY/...
Issued at 300 AM MDT Fri Oct 30 2026

A complex storm system will bring a change in the weather for our 
area Sunday night into the early part of next week. This will be a 
fairly large and potent weather system, but two or even three upper 
distinct upper level low pressure systems moving across the west 
will make for a very messy setup. While a deep but somewhat narrow 
trough approaches from the west, another moisture-laden system will 
race into southern California along a potent sub-tropical jet 
stream. This system will get pulled into or around the primary 
trough as it moves through the area. Meanwhile, there is potential 
for another upper level low over the northern Rockies to drop down 
simultaneously, interfering further with each system. While moisture 
will once again be extremely abundant (NAEFS mean precipitable water 
values exceed the 99th percentile of climatology Sunday night!), 
this system will have the same issue as most others this fall: 
a lack of strong forcing to actually extract this moisture as 
precipitation. 

Recent model guidance has trended largely towards the scenario where 
each of these upper level low pressure systems remain independent, 
with their forcing and lift interfering with one another. The 
overall evolution of the storm system has also trended more 
progressive and faster The net impact for our area is a decrease in 
the probability for widespread precipitation. While most areas can 
still expect some rain/snow showers with this event, the most likely 
scenario for QPF is fairly modest at this time. Greater than 75% of 
ensemble members have QPF under 0.25" for most areas inside a 
roughly Laramie to Glendo to Sidney triangle. There is still 
potential for between 0.25" and 0.75" liquid precipitation in Carbon 
county and along the Douglas to Chadron corridor, where forcing may 
be slightly more favorable. Still, about 25% of ensemble members 
keep the storm system too disorganized to deliver decent 
precipitation even to the Douglas to Chadron corridor, leaving most 
of the High Plains dry. Overall, confidence in expected QPF is 
highest for Carbon county at this time. There, extremely moist 
southwest flow can produce favorable orographic lift in the first 
phase of the storm system Sunday night into Monday morning, even if 
the second phase (the potential for wrap-around moisture) fails to 
materialize. Temperatures will be quite warm in advance of this 
system, meaning that snow levels will probably be as high as 9000 
ft. Snow levels will gradually fall Sunday night and Monday, but 
there is a bit of uncertainty in seeing any precipitation at all 
after the colder airmass moves into the area. Probabilities for 
advisory criteria snowfall remain around 50/50 in the Snowy and
Sierra Madre ranges, and about 25% in the northern Laramie 
range. 

Regardless of the precipitation outcome, a cold front will sweep 
through the area Sunday night and cooler and windier conditions for 
most areas on Monday. Look for a rapid increase in northwest winds 
Monday morning behind the frontal boundary. There is fairly high 
confidence in widespread wind gusts of 40 to 55 mph along and east 
of the Laramie Range through much of the day Monday. Most of these 
areas have about a 20 to 30% chance for winds exceeding high wind 
criteria at this time. Temperatures will actually be several degrees 
below seasonal averages, only reaching the mid to upper 40s for most 
areas. Tuesday will bring temperatures closer to seasonal averages 
and continued northwest winds, but they should not be as strong as 
Monday. 

Midweek onwards, disorganized ridging is expected to build back into 
the area. Temperatures look generally close to remain fairly close 
to seasonal averages with lighter winds, though breezy conditions 
may remain in the typical wind prone areas. There is potential for 
at least one if not two additional closed low systems later in the 
week towards next weekend, which may bring another chance for 
precipitation. However, confidence is extremely low at this lead 
time.
